parsed.summary: The file defines the k-colour triangle Ramsey number R_k(3) as the least n such that every k-colouring of K_n has a monochromatic triangle. It then states four consequences of the paper's result: R_k(3)^{1/k} → ∞, log R_k ~ k log k up to the constants 1/3 and 1, and log R_k = Θ(k log k). The main caveat is that `erdos_problem_183_explicit` has the false hypothesis `(1:ℕ)=0`, so it is vacuously true and says nothing about the explicit lower bound. Theorem 1.1 itself (existence of c with R_k(3) ≥ (c k^{1/3}/log k)^k for all k ≥ 2) has no faithful non-vacuous formalization.

glossary.plain: A k-edge-colouring C of K_n has no monochromatic triangle: each colour class graph is K_3-free.
glossary.standard_concept: triangle-free (no monochromatic triangle) k-colouring of K_n

glossary.plain: Every k-colouring of the edges of K_n contains a monochromatic triangle.
glossary.note: For k = 0 and n ≥ 2 there are no labelings, so the statement holds vacuously and gives junk R_0 = 2. This is irrelevant to the asymptotic statements.

glossary.plain: R_k(3) = least n such that every k-colouring of K_n has a monochromatic triangle.
glossary.standard_concept: multicolour Ramsey number R(3,…,3) with k colours
glossary.note: sInf junk value 0 only arises if the set is empty. The set is nonempty by the factorial upper bound.

lean_claims.plain: Assuming the false hypothesis 1 = 0 (in ℕ), the following holds. For all k ≥ 2, ((1/(6e^38))·k^{1/3}/log k)^k ≤ R_k(3), and R_k(3)^{1/k} → ∞. This is vacuous.
For every ε > 0, for all sufficiently large k, (1/3 − ε)·k·log k ≤ log R_k(3) ≤ (1+ε)·k·log k.
log R_k(3) = Θ(k log k) as k → ∞.

paper_claims.plain: There is an absolute constant c > 0 such that for every k ≥ 2, R_k(3) ≥ (c k^{1/3}/log k)^k.
Combined with the factorial upper bound (2), k^{(1/3−o(1))k} ≤ R_k(3) ≤ k^{(1+o(1))k}, so R_k(3) = k^{Θ(k)}.

coverage.paper_ref: Theorem 1.1 (explicit lower bound for all k ≥ 2)
coverage.why: The statement is guarded by the false hypothesis (1:ℕ)=0, so it carries no content. The explicit constant 1/(6e^38) is also not in the excerpt. No unconditional existence statement of c is formalized.
The ε-form with log is the standard reading of the o(1) exponents. It is unconditional.
log R_k = Θ(k log k) is equivalent to R_k = k^{Θ(k)}.
The statement is exactly that R_k(3)^{1/k} tends to infinity.

flags.explanation: The hypothesis h_mut : (1:ℕ) = 0 is false, so the theorem is vacuously true and proves nothing about the explicit bound. It is not a faithful rendering of Theorem 1.1. The explicit constant 1/(6e^38) is also not in the excerpt. If the explicit-constant statement is wanted, it should be stated without the hypothesis.
